dimensions.assessment: Affects federal law enforcement personnel, agencies, detainees, and individuals subject to immigration enforcement or border screening nationwide.
dimensions.evidence: This act provides $70 billion in funding to the Department of Homeland Security (DHS), U.S. Customs and Border Protection (CBP), and U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) through FY2029

dimensions.assessment: Substantially increases agency resources, personnel hiring, technology procurement, and detention or removal operations.
dimensions.evidence: There is appropriated to the Commissioner of U.S. Customs and Border Protection for fiscal year 2026, out of any money in the Treasury not otherwise appropriated, $9,550,000,000

dimensions.assessment: Appropriates $70 billion in federal funding through FY2029 and is designated to increase the deficit under reconciliation rules.
dimensions.evidence: This act provides $70 billion in funding to the Department of Homeland Security (DHS), U.S. Customs and Border Protection (CBP), and U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) through FY2029

dimensions.assessment: Directs extensive funding and statutory restrictions across multiple divisions of DHS, CBP, and ICE, including hiring mandates, technology deployment rules, and intergovernmental agreements.
dimensions.evidence: None of the funds made available under subsection (a) may be used for the procurement or deployment of surveillance towers along the southwest border and northern border that have not been tested

dimensions.assessment: Funds remain available until September 30, 2029, with permanent structural effects on agency operations and enforcement frameworks.
dimensions.evidence: to remain available until September 30, 2029, to hire, pay, train, and equip Border Patrol agents

importance_detail.rationale: This enacted legislation provides $70 billion in mandatory funding through fiscal year 2029 to the Department of Homeland Security, CBP, and ICE for border security, technology, personnel, and immigration enforcement.

summary: The Secure America Act provides $70 billion in total funding through fiscal year 2029 to the Department of Homeland Security, U.S. Customs and Border Protection, and U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement for border security, immigration enforcement, and related non-immigration missions.

affected_groups.effect: Receives billions in funding for personnel, equipment, technology, and non-immigration support.
Receives billions in funding for staff, investigations, detention and removal operations, legal staff, and state/local partnerships.
May participate in expanded 287(g) agreements and receive training regarding child exploitation and immigration enforcement.
affected_groups.group: State and local law enforcement agencies

key_provisions: Provides $9.55 billion to CBP for hiring, paying, training, and equipping Border Patrol agents and support personnel for functions other than immigration enforcement and customs.

Provides $7.45 billion to ICE for Homeland Security Investigations personnel and operations, including at least $108.5 million dedicated to child sexual exploitation and abuse victim identification and investigations.
Provides $3.45 billion to CBP for border technology, screening equipment, air and marine platforms, and biometric systems to combat illicit narcotics and drug trafficking.
Provides $13.02 billion to CBP for agent hiring, training, and operational support focused on immigration enforcement activities.

Provides $31.075 billion to ICE for immigration enforcement personnel, transportation, information technology, facility maintenance, 287(g) state and local agreements, legal staff, and targeted arrests of certain unlawful aliens.
missing_information: Exact overall deficit impact numbers beyond the general requirement that the reconciliation bill increases the deficit.
Specific staffing quotas or total numerical hiring targets for agents and personnel.
summary_detail.plain_summary: The Secure America Act provides $70 billion in total funding through fiscal year 2029 to the Department of Homeland Security, U.S. Customs and Border Protection, and U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement for border security, immigration enforcement, and related non-immigration missions.
summary_detail.significance: The Secure America Act directs $70 billion in federal appropriations across multiple sectors of the Department of Homeland Security to alter and expand operations regarding border security, drug interdiction, child exploitation investigations, and immigration enforcement through September 30, 2029.
